newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares drift lower, watching West.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares drift lower, watching West.

text.p: Russian shares opened weak on Monday and traders said investors were waiting for prices to drop further or were profit-taking.
The Russian Trading System (RTS) 23-share index started at 285.79 after Friday's closing 286.03, having drifted down from a February 20 high of 349.27. It was below 200 at the end of last year.
They predicted the market would keep quiet or drift lower for the next two weeks at least as Western markets remained nervous.
Alfa Capital trader Alexander Bubnovsky estimated that Russian shares were seeing a net outflow of capital as Western funds took profits in Russia to balance losses in world markets.
"People are on the sidelines waiting to see the correction in (Russian) prices due to corrections in the world indices," he said.
National utility UES EESR.RTS had fallen to $0.1855 at 0840 GMT from $0.1849 at Friday's close on the RTS. Regional power utility Mosenergo MSNG.RTS had fallen to $1.145 from $1.169.

Brunswick director Martin Diggle said a move by Mosenergo to limit outside control which will be voted on at a forthcoming shareholders meeting worried investors, as did possible restructuring of UES, a target of the new reform cabinet.
"People don't feel a compelling reason to invest today or this week," he said, adding that Wall Street jitters were keeping investor attention focused outside of Russia.
The Dow Jones industrial average rose 49 points on Friday, but ended the week down more than 214 points, close to the 216-point loss in the week to October 13, 1989.

A fall in U.S. unemployment and rise in wages in March have made some investors fear that interest rates, recently hiked 25 basis points, will go up again, and the bond market has been particularly hit.
"For four weeks we have seen no significant Western money coming into blue chips," Diggle said. "First we need stabilisation -- and I mean a week or two -- on Wall Street."
